findings.reason: an unnamed interval lets the worker build a guard whose window can be shorter than the restarted period, so the node's measure can pass while the 2026-10-13 case still reads healthy; naming an interval above the observed ~6.7 s (or comparing against a stored baseline rather than a second sample) changes what the node writes.
findings.text: §5's guard takes two restart-count readings "a few seconds apart", but §1 measures the cycle at one restart per ~6.7 s, so a sampled interval shorter than the period can read the same count on both samples and report the cycling unit healthy — the exact false negative §5 exists to remove

findings.reason: the overclaim is justification for hosting the reader on the manager, which is the right home regardless, so correcting it does not change what the node builds.
findings.text: §5's added sentence calls `SystemdUserUnitManager` the owner of "every systemd unit query" (reckon/service.py:324), but the repository reaches systemd directly elsewhere — `service.systemctl` in reckon/crew/paid_lanes.py:1147 and `service.write_named_unit` in the same module — so the manager is the per-unit query surface, not the sole systemd client

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — §5's cited surface resolves: `SystemdUserUnitManager` (reckon/service.py:324) with its `active()` (reckon/service.py:341), the `manager` seam `ensure_watcher_service` already takes (reckon/crew/watch_unit.py:384), and the `crew watch --ensure` caller (reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:2930); the extensionless hrefs resolve as `<path>.html` and the archive sections #s3/#s6 exist.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §5's done-when is a measurable two-arm test (rising count → cycling with both counts; holding count → reported as before, no added failure against base) and it declares a negative control (one reading only → healthy).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §5 cites no session-scratchpad or node-local path; its evidence is a test file under the repository's tests/ tree and the run directory convention the plan uses elsewhere.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §5's added text introduces no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags, and names behaviour (`a unit-property reader`, `cycling`) rather than a tracker item.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §5's two-reading detector can miss the very case it targets, because its sampling interval is left as "a few seconds" while its own §1 evidence measures a restart every ~6.7 s (see FINDING reasoning 1).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 carries one deliverable, reporting a cycling unit, and its "where the reader lives" clause is implementation guidance for that one goal, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — every relationship §5 declares is consistent: it names itself independent of §2 and its `data-links` is empty, and no depends-on it needs is missing.
